label: def:frobenius-dual-h3
title: Frobenius dual $K^\vee$ in $H_3(q)$
html:
Definition. Frobenius dual K^\vee in H_3(q)

Definition (Frobenius dual). Let G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(b_i \cdot b_j) be the (convention D: read on the quotient H_n/\mathrm{rad}\,\mathrm{tr}_M \cong \mathrm{TL}_n, where the induced pairing is non-degenerate; on H_n itself \det G = 0 exactly, the (1^3) block being the radical — MarkovGramDegenerate.lean) non-degenerate Frobenius Gram matrix on the NF basis \{b_i\} of H_3(q) (prop:frobenius-gram-matrix). For a state K = \sum_i c_i b_i in NF, the Frobenius dual is the unique element K^\vee \in H_3(q) satisfying \langle K^\vee, b_j \rangle_F = c_j for all j. Explicitly:

  K^\vee = \sum_{i,j} c_i (G^{-1})_{ij} b_j.

The dual exists and is unique by non-degeneracy of G — which under convention D holds on H_3/\mathrm{rad} \cong \mathrm{TL}_3 and not on H_3, where \det G = 0: the pairing \langle K^\vee, b_j \rangle_F = \sum_{i,k} c_i (G^{-1})_{ik} G_{kj} = \sum_i c_i \delta_{ij} = c_j follows from G^{-1} G = I.
